title: Introduce environment profiles and delta planner to reduce Terraform plan churn
creator: Liam Chen
description: Problem: frequent Terraform plan churn and noisy diffs are delaying safe rollouts and causing manual review overhead across environment overlays. Legacy networking templates embed provider pins and environment-specific knobs in multiple locations causing repeated state touches and long plans. Goal: refactor Terraform surface into declarative environment profiles (dev, staging, prod, regional overrides) and implement a lightweight 'delta planner' pre-step that computes minimal resource deltas and suggests targeted apply operations to reduce full-stack plan time and human review surface. Approach: 1) Introduce environment profile layer that centralizes provider versions, backend configs, and region mappings; 2) Extract networking blueprints into a registry of region-aware modules with explicit lifecycle knobs; 3) Implement delta-planner as a GitHub Actions/CI step that runs a drift-aware comparator and annotates PRs with expected impacted modules and estimated apply time; 4) Migrate a pilot workspace (staging in us-west-2) and validate plan reductions before broad rollout. Rollout plan includes detailed migration steps, schema migration tool for state moves, and a rollback strategy. Risks: state migration, accidental drifts during mass refactor, CI/perf regressions. Mitigations: staged migration, automated smoke applies to short-lived sandboxes, and a manual approval gate for initial production pilots.
acceptance_criteria: Environment profiles introduced and documented in infra repo with examples for dev/staging/prod
Delta planner CI step added that annotates PRs with impacted modules and an estimated apply time
Pilot migration completed for staging-us-west-2 with plan time reduction >= 50% for common change sets
State migration playbook and automated helper scripts exist and are validated in sandbox
No customer-facing incidents and rollback path validated in a dry-run apply
